fields.meta_title: Free Volunteer Form Builder With Signed Hour Logs | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a volunteer form that asks each role its own questions and logs hours a supervisor signs. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Volunteer Form That Places People and Proves Their Hours
fields.hero_description: Create a volunteer form that screens each applicant for the role they pick and counts only the hours a supervisor confirms.
fields.features_heading: What a Coordinator Gets Past the Sign-Up
fields.features_subheading: A volunteer program runs on what happens after someone applies. These six pieces cover the checks and the hours.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the role picked

Show each applicant only the questions for the role they choose. A weekend driver answers license and vehicle questions, while a reading tutor gives grade levels instead.
fields.feature_2:
Screening held until each step clears

Hold applicants at the checks your program requires, such as references or a background check. Coordinators see who waits on which step, and nobody is placed too early.
fields.feature_3:
Reference requests sent on submit

Email each listed reference a short form of their own when an application arrives. Their answers attach to the applicant's record, and a silent reference gets a reminder.
fields.feature_4:
Hours totaled by person and program

Add up every logged hour by volunteer and by program on one dashboard. Export one volunteer's history as a PDF when a school or scholarship committee asks to see it.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts for the applications that need you

Send the coordinator a Slack or email alert when someone applies for a role with open spots. Routine applications wait in the queue, and each alert links to the record.
fields.feature_6:
The volunteer app, exported as code

Export the full codebase to GitHub on paid plans when the form grows into a volunteer portal. A developer can extend it later without rebuilding the records you already hold.
fields.why_title: Why Build Volunteer Forms With Emergent?
fields.why_description: A template stops at the names. Emergent builds the steps a coordinator runs after each one and keeps a record per volunteer.

fields.tab_content_1:
Every hour on the log is signed for

Hollis High asks every senior for 40 service hours before graduation. Maya logs four hours shelving books at Larkfield Library from her phone. Her site supervisor, Dan Reyes, opens an email link and signs. Only then do the hours count, and her total on the counselor's dashboard moves from 28 to 32.
fields.tab_content_2:
Mentors matched after references and a background check

Brightpath pairs adults with middle schoolers for weekly one-on-one meetings. Its mentor application asks for two references, and each one gets a short form by email. When both have answered, the applicant moves to a background check. The coordinator can propose a match only after that step clears.
fields.tab_content_3:
Foster applicants answer six questions on their home

Volunteers at Cedar Row Animal Shelter pick a role first. Dog walkers then mark the weekday mornings they can cover. Choosing foster opens six more questions about the home, such as landlord approval and other pets. Foster applications skip the general queue and go to Priya, the foster coordinator.
fields.tab_content_4:
Sawyers within one county get the flood alert

When the river at Mill Ford crosses flood stage, Riverline Relief needs people who can clear fallen trees. Its volunteer form records certifications and home county. The coordinator filters the registry for chainsaw certification in Alder County and finds 14 volunteers. All of them get an email with the staging site.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Volunteer Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a volunteer form's roles, screening, and hour sign-off, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List every role and what it requires
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Set the screening steps for each role
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with what the volunteer will do. Write down each role with its own requirements: a minimum age, a driver's license, weekday mornings, a background check. The roles decide which questions appear, which is why this list comes before any field.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for contact details and the role first, nothing more. A person who has picked a role is more willing to answer the longer questions that follow it. Mark a field required only when a coordinator cannot place someone without it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask the questions a coordinator acts on, and match the checks to the risk. A one-day park cleanup may need nothing beyond contact details. A role with children or vulnerable adults usually needs references and a background check before placement.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Keep the reference form to four or five questions a reference can answer in two minutes. Ask how long they have known the applicant and whether they would trust them in this role. Leave one open box for anything else.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Signatures come from the supervisor at the site, not from the volunteer. Collect that person's name and email on each log entry. Hours stay pending until they confirm, and the total any school or employer sees counts confirmed hours only.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose the few events that need a person's attention, such as a reference who has not replied or an applicant for a hard-to-fill role. Send those to the coordinator by email or Slack. Leave everything else on the dashboard.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Apply once as a stranger would
fields.howto_step_7_des: Open the form on a phone with no saved logins and apply for the most demanding role. Use a friend as a reference to check the request arrives. Then log an hour, confirm it as the supervisor and watch the total change.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is template galleries (Jotform, Pinterest, pdfFiller), one signup-sheet service, a Microsoft Forms template, an Indeed how-to and a college's PDF hour log. Every one stops at the blank form. This page treats a volunteer form as the first record in a volunteer's file: the student whose hours only count once a supervisor signs, the mentor who cannot be matched until two references and a background check clear, the shelter applicant whose chosen role decides the questions, and the relief group that finds every certified sawyer in a county when a flood warning lands. The FAQ answers the PAA questions on proof of hours, filling a form in and applying, plainly.
tab_stories: A high school student logs four hours at the public library, the site supervisor confirms them from an email link with a signature, and the student's running total moves to 32 of the 40 hours the school requires.

A youth mentoring program accepts a mentor application, emails the two listed references for their answers and holds the applicant at a background check step before the coordinator can propose a match.

An animal shelter's form changes with the role picked: dog walkers answer weekday availability while foster applicants answer six questions about their home and pets and go straight to the foster coordinator.

A disaster relief group keeps a skills registry from its volunteer form, and when a flood warning is issued the coordinator filters for chainsaw-certified volunteers in one county and emails all 14 of them.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Volunteer Form That Places People and Proves Their Hours', meta title 'Free Volunteer Form Builder With Signed Hour Logs | Emergent' and hero 'Create a volunteer form that screens each applicant for the role they pick and counts only the hours a supervisor confirms.' cover applying, screening and hours; how-to description is one sentence under 140 characters.

intent.evidence: Builder-fit SERP of template galleries and builders: the FAQ covers what goes on the form, filling one out, student forms, templates and sign-up forms; the how-to plans roles, screening, references and hour sign-off; the table compares the builders that rank.

specificity.evidence: Coordinator vocabulary: 'site supervisor', 'background check', 'foster coordinator', 'staging site', '40 service hours before graduation'.

openers.evidence: Full-sentence openers: 'Hollis High asks every senior for 40 service hours before graduation.', 'Signatures come from the supervisor at the site, not from the volunteer.'; feature bodies open on verbs (Show, Hold, Email, Add, Send, Export).

craft.evidence: Varied sentences ending on the point ('Only then do the hours count'); one 'which is why' ending and repeated ideas logged as notes.

voice.evidence: Concrete details: 'her total on the counselor's dashboard moves from 28 to 32', 'filters the registry for chainsaw certification in Alder County and finds 14 volunteers'.

truth.evidence: Waiver definition and state-law enforceability, mentor screening and supervisor-signed hour logs map to domain_sources; Emergent claims (no response cap, database you own, alerts, e-signature, code export on paid plans, free to start) are approved; images agree (28 + 4 = 32 of 40, 2 of 2 references, 14 volunteers).

distinct.evidence: No sibling primary in a heading; background-check-form and sign-up-form are linked, not targeted; the foster tab is a volunteer role, not the pet adoption page's topic.

faq.evidence: 10 items, answer-first, hub link in item 2, exact-match links to background-check-form and sign-up-form, no brand or file format in any question, moat lines in items 6, 7 and 9.

images.evidence: Tab 1 Larkfield Library, 4 hours, signed by Dan Reyes, total 28 to 32, goal 40; tab 2 Brightpath, references 2 of 2, background check in progress, match locked; tab 3 fosters routed to Priya with 6 home questions; tab 4 14 chainsaw-certified volunteers in Alder County emailed the Mill Ford staging site.
